calls.evidence: FACT - the response was observed (HTTP status and rate-limit headers recorded here) but its body is not persisted in this artifact; only the fields quoted in _capture.notes survive. Not reconstructed, and not substituted from any other artifact. See _capture.omissions.

tooling.curl: curl 8.14.1 (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu) libcurl/8.14.1 OpenSSL/3.5.3 zlib/1.3.1 brotli/1.1.0 zstd/1.5.7 libidn2/2.3.8 libpsl/0.21.2 libssh2/1.11.1 nghttp2/1.64.0 librtmp/2.3 OpenLDAP/2.6.10

notes: FACT: `. /etc/profile.d/blitzy-cobolcheck-env.sh` was issued as the literal first command of this run, guarded by a file-existence test so that a missing script could not abort the run. The script is present in this container and sourced with exit status 0; this capture requires only curl and python3, both already on PATH.

FACT: tool versions in `tooling` are read from this container at assembly time rather than transcribed, and two contradictions of the values named in the task description are recorded there rather than repeated here: the observed python3 and curl versions differ from the ones it named, and jq is present where it stated jq was absent from the image. gh is absent. Nothing was installed; the capture is driven by python3 as instructed.

FACT: GET https://api.github.com/rate_limit returned HTTP 200 with an observed x-ratelimit-limit ceiling of 5000 and x-ratelimit-remaining of 5000. `authenticated` is derived from that observed ceiling alone (5000 means authenticated, 60 means unauthenticated) and never from the presence of a token variable.

FACT: the comments endpoint was requested with per_page=100 and paginated by traversing the Link rel="next" relation to exhaustion. 1 page(s) were fetched, the final `link_next` is null, and 5 comment record(s) were returned with HTTP 200.

FACT: https://api.github.com/repos/openmainframeproject/cobol-check/issues?state=open&per_page=100 returned 53 entries; filtering on the ABSENCE of a `pull_request` key yields exactly 45 true issues and 8 pull-request entries, which matches the carried-forward ground truth of 45 open issues and 8 open pull requests and so validates the filter rather than assuming it.
FACT: every comment object and the `issue` payload are stored exactly as returned by the API. No field was pruned, truncated, re-wrapped, re-rendered, HTML-stripped or whitespace-normalised.

FACT: every entry in `calls` carries method "GET"; the capture driver contains no code path capable of issuing POST, PATCH, PUT or DELETE, and no comment, reaction, label, assignment, reopen or edit was attempted. The target repository is archived and read-only.

FACT: the repository identity is hard-pinned to openmainframeproject/cobol-check. No URL in `calls` contains the string "neopragma"; the wiki link at README.md:L38 is a misdirection and was never used, while README.md:L42 and README.md:L55 carry the correct owner.

FACT: the API credential was read only from os.environ inside the capture process and placed only into an in-memory request header. It appears in no file, filename, log line or process argument list, and no request header was echoed.

FACT - the raw response body of the second open-issues listing recorded in _capture.calls, GET https://api.github.com/repos/openmainframeproject/cobol-check/issues?state=open&per_page=100, is NOT retained in this artifact; it returned 53 entries and only the two resolution fields quoted in these notes survive. The canonical persisted capture of that same endpoint is upstream-harvest/issues.json, which is what a consumer must read; this duplicate call's body must not be reconstructed and re-querying is prohibited because the upstream repository is archived and read-only. _capture.omissions records the gap.

FACT: CREDENTIAL TRANSPORT — the HTTP client recorded for this artifact is python3 `urllib.request` at `_capture.tooling.capture_driver`, which runs in process: the credential was read from the environment and set as a request header inside the capture process, so it entered no process argument vector. The classification is machine-readable at `_capture.credential_transport_exposure = "in_process_client_only"`. No credential value, header or fragment appears anywhere in this artifact at rest, and every call in `_capture.calls` is a `GET`. The transport rule binding any future authenticated capture is fixed in `upstream-harvest/HARVEST-MANIFEST.md` section 3.3.1.

FACT: PUBLIC-DATA GOVERNANCE — this artifact retains public GitHub records verbatim, including contributor `login`, profile and avatar URLs, timestamps and comment bodies, because it is the audit copy of a one-time capture against an archived repository and fidelity is its purpose. Use of that data is bounded to backlog triage and provenance audit for this programme. The binding purpose, access and publication boundary, retention trigger, disposal rule, deleted-upstream-content handling and the prohibition on profiling, enrichment, outreach and every other secondary use are stated in `upstream-harvest/HARVEST-MANIFEST.md` section 12. Those rules constrain use and lifetime; they never license editing this evidence.

flagged_issue_resolution.description: The SonarQube-output issue, flagged by description only and never by number in the carried-forward ground truth, which removes the org.sonarqube 3.0 plugin entirely rather than bumping it.
flagged_issue_resolution.cited_title: Produce Sonarqube formatted output for test results.
flagged_issue_resolution.evidence: FACT: a mechanical case-insensitive scan of all 45 harvested true-issue titles and labels from https://api.github.com/repos/openmainframeproject/cobol-check/issues?state=open&per_page=100 for /sonar|static[- ]?analys|code quality|quality gate/ returned exactly one candidate: issue number 150, harvested title verbatim 'Produce Sonarqube formatted output for test results.', harvested labels ['enhancement', 'good first issue']. The harvested title itself carries the SonarQube-formatted-output wording that the description denotes, so the citation is the title and not an interpretation of it. FACT: the title agrees across two independent GET calls, the list endpoint and https://api.github.com/repos/openmainframeproject/cobol-check/issues/150, so the citation is corroborated rather than single-sourced. FACT: exactly one candidate means the ambiguity rule is not engaged.

flagged_issue_resolution.description: The build-numbers issue, flagged by description only and never by number in the carried-forward ground truth, arising from the two CHANGELOG.md entries both numbered 0.2.19 that must be reconciled.
flagged_issue_resolution.cited_title: Add autoincremented build numbers to the gradle build
flagged_issue_resolution.evidence: FACT: issue number 93 in the harvest from https://api.github.com/repos/openmainframeproject/cobol-check/issues?state=open&per_page=100 carries the title verbatim 'Add autoincremented build numbers to the gradle build' with harvested labels ['enhancement', 'good first issue', 'infrastructure']; the title contains the literal phrase "build numbers", which is the citation this resolution rests on. FACT: a deliberately broad case-insensitive scan of all 45 harvested true-issue titles and labels for /build[\s\-_]*number|\bversion|\bversioning|release[\s\-_]*number|semver|auto[\s\-_]?increment|\bnumbering/ returned two candidates, number 93 and number 343 whose harvested title is verbatim 'FreeBSD version in wiki does not make sens'; a scan narrowed to numbering of the product's builds or releases, /build[\s\-_]*number|release[\s\-_]*number|version[\s\-_]*number|auto[\s\-_]?increment/, returned only number 93. INFERENCE: number 343 is a match on the bare word "version" alone; its harvested title scopes it to a FreeBSD release recorded in the project wiki and contains no build-, release- or version-numbering wording for this product, so it is not a plausible second reading of the description and the ambiguity rule is not engaged. Both candidates are quoted here verbatim so the determination stays checkable. FACT: the title of number 93 agrees across two independent GET calls, the list endpoint and https://api.github.com/repos/openmainframeproject/cobol-check/issues/93.
